attributes.description: Alerts when the proportion of ERROR or WARNING level log entries for a given log source exceeds 10% over a 15-minute window. Catches recoverable issues and caught exceptions that don't necessarily surface as an HTTP 5xx.
attributes.name: [Vercel OTel] Elevated ERROR/WARNING log rate by source

investigation_guide.blob:
## Elevated ERROR/WARNING Log Rate

### Triage Steps
1. Note the affected `vercel.log.source` from the alert context (typically `lambda` or `edge`).
2. Inspect recent error/warning messages: `FROM logs-vercel.logs.otel-default | WHERE vercel.log.source == "<source>" AND log.level IN ("ERROR", "WARNING") | KEEP @timestamp, log.level, message, http.route, deployment.id | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 50`
3. Group messages to find the dominant error signature — a single recurring exception usually indicates a specific code defect introduced by a recent deployment.
4. Cross-check against the HTTP 5xx error rate rule — if this rule fires but the 5xx rule does not, the application may be catching and logging errors without surfacing them to the client, which can still indicate a degraded experience.

### Note
This is a count-based proportion of raw log entries, not tied to HTTP status codes — it will catch issues in `stdout`/`stderr` output that never produce a bad response.

### Escalation
If the elevated rate persists for more than 30 minutes or is accompanied by a rising 5xx rate, escalate to the on-call engineer.

esqlQuery.esql:
FROM logs-vercel.logs.otel-default
| WHERE deployment.environment.name == "production"
| STATS
    total = COUNT(*),
    bad = COUNT(*) WHERE log.level IN ("ERROR", "WARNING")
  BY vercel.log.source
// Minimum sample size to avoid noisy alerts on low-traffic sources
| WHERE total > 20
| EVAL bad_rate_pct = ROUND(TO_DOUBLE(bad) / total * 100.0, 2)
// WARNING entries are expected to be more frequent than hard errors, so this threshold is set higher
// than the 5xx error-rate rule. Lower it if your application logs WARNING sparingly.
| WHERE bad_rate_pct > 10.0
| SORT bad_rate_pct DESC
| LIMIT 10
